7.03.b:
### Hold it → side
- Plateau **up**, **tibial tuberosity** facing **away** from you (anterior)
- **Medial plateau** → larger, oval, **concave**
- **Lateral plateau** → smaller, round, **convex**
- **Fibular facet** → under the lateral condyle, posterolateral
- **Gerdy's tubercle** → anterolateral → iliotibial band
- Side rule → tuberosity forward, find the fibular facet → that side is lateral

### Point & say — the plateau map (front → back)
- Order → **M-A-L | L-M-P** → see the pin map
  [[FIG: Fig 7.8, 7.9 · 7.03
  - **M** → anterior horn of **medial** meniscus (most anterior)
  - **A** → **ACL** footprint
  - **L** → anterior horn of **lateral** meniscus (fibres blend with ACL)
  - Tibial spines (medial and lateral intercondylar tubercles)
  - **L** → posterior horn of lateral meniscus
  - **M** → posterior horn of medial meniscus
  - **P** → **PCL** → posterior sulcus, below the joint line
- ACL tibial centre → **≈7.5 mm medial** to anterior horn of lateral meniscus; **≈7 mm anterior** to PCL
- Posterior root of medial meniscus → **≈8 mm** from PCL → protect it when drilling PCL tunnel

### Point & say — around the tibia
- Muscle map of tibia and fibula → origins red, insertions blue
  [[FIG: Fig 7.10 · 7.03
- **Tibial tuberosity** → patellar tendon; ≈3 cm below joint line
- **Gerdy's tubercle** → ITB; also origin of tibialis anterior
- **Medial flare** → pes anserinus (Sartorius, Gracilis, semiTendinosus → "Say Grace before Tea")
  - Deep and posterior to pes → **distal sMCL** (≈6 cm below joint)
- **Posteromedial groove** → semimembranosus (direct arm)

- **Posterior surface** → popliteus (triangle above soleal line) → **soleal line** → soleus
- **Posterior intercondylar fossa** → PCL (champagne-glass drop-off)
- **Posterior slope** of the plateau ≈7–10° (Netter) → steeper → more anterior tibial shear → a cause of **failed ACL** reconstruction
- **Nutrient foramen** → back of the tibia just below the soleal line → the **largest nutrient artery** in the body (posterior tibial), running **downward** → the distal third gets the least
- **Shaft** → **triangular** in section with a subcutaneous anteromedial face (Netter) → a **narrow** plate sits on it (round humerus → broad plate)

CLINICAL PEARL — around the tibia

- **Pes anserine bursa** → between the pes tendons and the distal sMCL → tender **below** the joint line, over the pes → not the meniscus
- **Lateral plateau fractures > medial** (Netter) → convex lateral plateau, overhanging with less metaphyseal support and weaker trabeculae; valgus blows are commoner; the LFC strikes it
- Role of the **MCL** → intact → hinge → LFC acts as a **chisel** → **split**; torn → LFC acts as a **hammer** → **depression** (oral-questions collection)
- **Distal third** heals slowly → end of the nutrient supply + thin soft-tissue cover

### Point & say — fibular head
- Map → three pins on the head + one danger band on the neck (pin map above)
- **LCL** → lateral fibular head, ≈8 mm behind its anterior margin
- **Biceps femoris** → fibular head, wraps around LCL ("V" on sagittal MRI)
- **Styloid (apex)** → popliteofibular ligament, fabellofibular, arcuate ligaments
- **Fibular neck** → **common peroneal nerve** winds around it → palpable
- Soleus → posterior fibular head; peroneus longus → lateral head and shaft

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "what attaches to the fibular head?" (Prof. Shamaa)
- Lateral face, ≈8 mm behind the front → **FCL**
- Wrapping round the FCL → **biceps femoris** (its main insertion)
- **Styloid** (apex, posterior) → **popliteofibular**, fabellofibular and arcuate ligaments
- Back → **soleus**; side and shaft → **peroneus longus**; front → EDL
- Neck → **common peroneal nerve**; medial facet → proximal tibiofibular joint

- Fibular head avulsion on X-ray → **arcuate sign** → posterolateral corner until proved otherwise
- Do not confuse it with a Segond fracture → lateral **tibial** rim (ALL / capsule) → ACL
- The oral-questions collection puts biceps + LCL on the "tip" and the PFL, fabellofibular and arcuate on the "lateral margin" → cadaveric data (LaPrade 2003): FCL on the lateral head, biceps round it, the three ligaments on the **styloid**

7.04.b:
### Capsule and synovial reflections
- Femur → synovium attaches at the **edge of the articular cartilage**; anteriorly it is lifted up as the **suprapatellar pouch** (a bursa that joins the joint)
  [[FIG: Fig 7.11 · 7.04
- **Anterior capsule** is replaced by the quadriceps tendon, patella, patellar tendon and retinacula; **posterior capsule** is thick → strengthened by the **OPL**
- Openings / communications → suprapatellar pouch, **popliteus** tendon (hiatus), **gastrocnemius–semimembranosus** bursa (Baker's cyst)
- Inside the capsule, outside the synovium → **cruciates**, **popliteus tendon**, **infrapatellar (Hoffa's) fat pad**
- Knee metaphyses are **extracapsular** → unlike the hip, shoulder, elbow and ankle, metaphyseal osteomyelitis does not spill straight into the knee
- Effusion fills the suprapatellar pouch first → ballottement; aspirate superolateral, into the pouch

### Synovial folds (plicae)
- **Infrapatellar plica = ligamentum mucosum** → fat pad to the notch, in front of the ACL → debride to see the ACL (Netter)
  [[FIG: Fig 7.12 · 7.04
- **Medial (shelf) plica** → the symptomatic one → sweeps over the medial femoral condyle at ≈30° (Netter)
- **Suprapatellar** plica → usually silent; **lateral** plica → rare

| Bone | Secondary centre appears | Fuses | Point to say |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Distal femur** | **At birth** (present in a term newborn) | ≈19 y | **Fastest physis** → ≈7 mm/yr (Netter), ≈70% of femoral length |
| **Proximal tibia** | At / just before birth | ≈18–20 y | ≈55–60% of tibial length; **tuberosity** = anterior tongue of the epiphysis |
| **Tibial tuberosity** | ≈10–12 y | with the proximal tibia | Open apophysis → **Osgood–Schlatter** |
| **Proximal fibula** | ≈3–4 y (late) | ≈18–20 y | Breaks the rule (below) |
| **Patella** | ≈3 y (Netter) | — | Several centres → unfused **superolateral** → bipartite |
